title: Podcast pilot script: Winter in Central Indiana and your 2027 move
hook: The last time this show was on the air, we asked whether you should wait to make an offer. Ten years later, it's still the question we hear most.
body:
# Indianapolis Real Estate Podcast with the Evelo Team
## Pilot: Winter in Central Indiana: what the latest numbers mean for your 2027 move

Runtime target: about 14 minutes. Record December 9, 2026. Release January 6, 2027.

> **PRODUCER NOTE:** The four market numbers in this episode (homes for sale, days on market, price-cut share, 30-year rate) are October data, the latest at recording. Before the January 6 release, refresh them to November data from the same sources, record the changed lines as pickups, and update the show notes to match.

## Outline
- **00:00** Cold open: the show is back
- **00:40** Welcome: meet the host and first guest
- **01:45** Segment 1: What the market feels like right now
- **05:00** Segment 2: Then vs now: "Should You Wait to Make an Offer in Indianapolis?" (June 2016)
- **08:15** Segment 3: Planning a 2027 move, for buyers and sellers
- **11:00** Segment 4: The giving plan behind every closing
- **13:00** Wrap, one next step and end card

## Script

**00:00 Cold open**

[HOST] The last time this show was on the air, we asked whether you should wait to make an offer. Ten years later, it's still the question we hear most. So we're bringing the show back to answer it properly.

[MUSIC IN, THEN UNDER]

**00:40 Welcome**

[HOST] Welcome back to the Indianapolis Real Estate Podcast with the Evelo Team. I'm {HOST_FIRST_NAME}, and I lead one of our teams here in Fishers. I talked {GUEST_FIRST_NAME} into being the first guest of the reboot.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] You didn't have to talk very hard. I listened to a couple of the 2016 episodes to prep.

[HOST] And?

[GUEST: Evelo agent] The audio has aged. The questions haven't. People still want to know when to buy, when to sell, and whether they're about to make a mistake.

[HOST] That's the whole idea. Every other Wednesday: one real question, a little local data, plain English. No lectures.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] I can do no lectures.

**01:45 Segment 1: What the market feels like right now**

[HOST] You're in homes most weekends. What feels different from a year ago?

[GUEST: Evelo agent] Choice. A year ago, a lot of buyers felt like they were fighting over a short list. Now they have room to compare.

[HOST] And the data backs that up. We're recording in December, so these are October numbers from Realtor.com via FRED, the latest we have. Hamilton County had 1,111 homes for sale. That's up about 19% from a year earlier.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] And they're taking a bit longer to sell. The typical Hamilton County listing sat 49 days on the market, up from 45 a year ago.

[HOST] So what does that look like at a showing?

[GUEST: Evelo agent] Calmer. Fewer cars in the driveway at the same time. Buyers can go home, sleep on it and come back for a second look.

[HOST] Sellers are feeling it too.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] They are. Across the Indianapolis metro, more than half of the homes for sale in October had a price cut at some point. That's not a crisis. Usually it means the first price was set for a market that had already moved.

[HOST] And then there's the number everybody asks me about at dinner parties.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] Rates. Freddie Mac's 30-year average was 7.28% the week of November 19. Higher than a year ago.

[HOST] So: more homes, more time, plenty of price cuts, and pricier borrowing. That's the backdrop. Now the real question.

**05:00 Segment 2: Then vs now**

[HOST] In June 2016, we recorded an episode called "Should You Wait to Make an Offer in Indianapolis?" I'm not going to play it for you. Trust me on that.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] That's a kindness.

[HOST] But the title holds up. So, then versus now. If a buyer asks you that today, what do you say?

[GUEST: Evelo agent] I ask which wait they mean, because there are two. One is waiting a few days on a specific house. The other is waiting on the whole move.

[HOST] Start with the house.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] On a single house, you usually have more room than people think right now. Homes are sitting longer, so you can see it twice, read the disclosures and know your payment before you write anything. That isn't stalling. That's homework.

[HOST] Okay. Waiting on the whole move.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] That one's personal. Nobody can tell you where rates go next, and I'd be careful with anyone who says they can. If you wait for spring, you'll probably see more listings, and more buyers along with them. So I ask, "Wait for what, exactly?" A rate? A job change? A bonus? If you can name it, we can plan around it.

[HOST] Then versus now, in one line.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] Then: should you wait? Now: know what you're waiting for.

**08:15 Segment 3: Planning a 2027 move**

[HOST] Let's make it practical. Say I want to buy in Fishers or Noblesville in 2027. Where do I start?

[GUEST: Evelo agent] With a lender, before the listing apps. Get pre-approved so you know your payment at today's rate, not the price you hope for. Then use the extra choice. Tour more homes than you think you need, and ask your agent for each home's price history.

[HOST] And when you find the one?

[GUEST: Evelo agent] Remember the negotiation is bigger than price. Repairs, closing costs, move-in timing. In a calmer market, those become real conversations.

[HOST] Now flip it. I'm selling in Carmel or Westfield.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] Price for the market you're in, not the one your neighbor sold in. Buyers have options, so the first couple of weeks matter most. Clean, repaired, well photographed and priced with current data. And plan for a longer timeline than you might expect.

**11:00 Segment 4: The giving plan**

[HOST] Before we wrap, something close to home for us. The very last episode we posted in 2016 was called "Support Your Local Food Pantry." It felt wrong to bring the show back without that part.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] It's one of my favorite things about this team. Our agents give part of their commission from every closing to KW Cares, the REALTOR Foundation and Filter of Hope. Filter of Hope provides household water filters for people living in poverty.

[HOST] And to be clear, that comes from us. Not from our clients, and not from the sale price.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] Right. Nobody pays a cent extra for it.

[HOST] We've helped more than 2,500 clients move since 1998. Today, every closing also does a little good somewhere else. Starting this season, each episode ends with a short spotlight on a Central Indiana nonprofit.

**13:00 Wrap**

[HOST] Quick recap. More homes for sale, more time to decide, and higher rates than a year ago. If you're weighing a 2027 move, the first step is a short conversation.

[GUEST: Evelo agent] And you don't need it all figured out before you call. That's what the call is for.

[HOST] Call us at 317-863-9011 and ask for a 2027 move plan. See you in two weeks.

[MUSIC UP]

**End card (read over music)**

[HOST] The Indianapolis Real Estate Podcast is produced by the Evelo Team | Keller Williams Indy Metro NE. Each office is independently owned and operated. Market data from Realtor.com via FRED and Freddie Mac via FRED, the latest available at recording. This episode is general information, not financial advice.

# Episode 1: Winter in Central Indiana: what the latest numbers mean for your 2027 move

**Indianapolis Real Estate Podcast with the Evelo Team** | Released January 6, 2027 | About 14 minutes

## Summary
Should you wait to move in 2027? Ten years after we first asked it on this show, we answer it again. A team leader and an Evelo agent talk through what the Hamilton County market feels like right now, then revisit our June 2016 episode "Should You Wait to Make an Offer in Indianapolis?" The short answer: know what you're waiting for. They share practical first steps for buyers and sellers planning a 2027 move, and explain how our agents give part of their commission from every closing to KW Cares, the REALTOR Foundation and Filter of Hope.

## Key numbers from the episode
October data, the latest at recording:
- Hamilton County homes for sale: 1,111, up 19.3% from a year earlier
- Hamilton County median days on market: 49, up from 45
- Metro listings with a price cut: more than half (55.4%)
- 30-year fixed mortgage rate: 7.28% (week of November 19, 2026)

Sources: Realtor.com via FRED, October 2026; Freddie Mac via FRED, week of November 19, 2026.

## Timestamps
- 00:00 Cold open: the show is back
- 00:40 Welcome
- 01:45 What the market feels like right now
- 05:00 Then vs now: "Should You Wait to Make an Offer in Indianapolis?"
- 08:15 Planning a 2027 move
- 11:00 The giving plan behind every closing
- 13:00 Wrap

## Links
- Evelo Team: [eveloteam.com](https://www.eveloteam.com)
- Blog: [eveloteam.com/blog](https://www.eveloteam.com/blog)
- Related post: [Should I Wait to Buy a House Until Interest Rates Drop More?](https://www.eveloteam.com/blog/should-i-wait-to-buy-until-interest-rates-drop)
- Related post: [What Is the Housing Market Like in Fishers Right Now?](https://www.eveloteam.com/blog/fishers-indiana-housing-market)
- Our giving plan: [eveloteam.com/giving](https://www.eveloteam.com/giving)

## Talk with us
Weighing a move in Fishers, Carmel, Noblesville, Westfield or anywhere in Hamilton County? Call 317-863-9011 and ask for a 2027 move plan.

body:
# Indianapolis Real Estate Podcast with the Evelo Team: Season 1 plan (January to March 2027)

**Suggested next step:** a 20-minute planning call to walk through this plan and lock in the December 9 pilot recording.

One 45-minute recording every two weeks gives us a podcast episode, 4 clips, a blog post, a newsletter feature and a Google Business Profile post. The show already has a feed and a back catalog from 2016, so we restart with an audience path in place instead of starting from zero.

**Format:** 12-15 minutes, released every other Wednesday. Host: a team leader. One guest per episode. Each episode answers one real question with local data, revisits a 2016 episode where it fits, and closes with a 1-minute Central Indiana nonprofit spotlight.

## Episodes

### Ep 1 | January 6, 2027 | Winter in Central Indiana: what the latest numbers mean for your 2027 move
Premise: The pilot, recorded December 9 with October data (the latest at recording), refreshed to November data before release.
We revisit "Should You Wait to Make an Offer in Indianapolis?" as then vs now and introduce the giving plan.
Guest type: Evelo agent.

### Ep 2 | January 20, 2027 | Is it better to buy than rent in Hamilton County in 2027?
Premise: We revisit our 2016 rent vs buy episode with current rates and list prices.
We walk through the questions that decide it: how long you'll stay, your budget and your down payment.
Guest type: local mortgage lender.

### Ep 3 | February 3, 2027 | How do I prepare my home to sell this spring?
Premise: The 2016 spring prep episode, updated for a market with more homes for sale.
What to fix, what to skip, and how presentation affects time on market.
Guest type: home stager.

### Ep 4 | February 17, 2027 | New construction in Fishers, Noblesville and Westfield: what to ask a builder
Premise: Builder contracts, incentives and timelines, explained in plain English.
How a buyer's agent helps on a new build, and when to bring one in.
Guest type: the team's new construction specialist.

### Ep 5 | March 3, 2027 | The home inspection, ten years later
Premise: Our 2016 episode made the case for a three-part home inspection.
We ask what a thorough inspection covers today and how to use the report in negotiation.
Guest type: licensed home inspector.

### Ep 6 | March 17, 2027 | How should sellers weigh offers this spring?
Premise: Price is only one part of an offer. Terms, financing and timing matter too.
We revisit the 2016 multiple-offers episode and update it with spring 2027 data.
Guest type: Evelo listing agent.

## Production workflow (repeats every two weeks)

1. **Plan (Thursday after each release):** Pick the question from client calls, blog comments and search trends. Pull the latest numbers (Realtor.com via FRED, Freddie Mac via FRED) and label them with the month they cover. Write a one-page outline. Run a fair housing and data check before recording.
2. **Record (the Wednesday between releases):** About 45 minutes in the Fishers office, two mics and two cameras so the video works for YouTube and clips. Guest gets the outline 48 hours ahead.
3. **Edit (within 48 hours):** Cut to 12-15 minutes. Add intro music, the spoken end card with "Evelo Team | Keller Williams Indy Metro NE," and a transcript. Refresh any number that aged since recording. Team leader approves the final cut.
4. **Clip (same day as edit):** Cut 4 vertical clips of 30-45 seconds each. Hook in the first 3 seconds, one number at most, burned-in captions, a source tag on screen and a brokerage end card. Schedule to Instagram Reels, Facebook, YouTube Shorts and LinkedIn across the two weeks.
5. **Publish (release Wednesday, morning):** Post to Apple Podcasts (existing show feed), Spotify and the Evelo Team YouTube channel. Show notes include a summary, timestamps, sources and links to eveloteam.com and the blog.
6. **Repurpose to blog (release Wednesday):** Turn the transcript into the week's question-style blog post on eveloteam.com/blog, with the episode embedded. Feature it in the next email newsletter and a Google Business Profile post.
7. **Review (Friday after each release):** Track downloads, clip views, blog visits, and calls or emails that mention the show. Keep what works and adjust the next outline.

Evelo Team | Keller Williams Indy Metro NE. Each office is independently owned and operated.
